anomaly_def.Name: Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The log-write, flush, switch, or archive path on the primary instance cannot sustain the redo generation rate, so commit processing stalls on log-related waits and space shortages.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly: Standbys or downstream consumers fall behind because they cannot receive, persist, or apply the primary’s log stream fast enough, causing growing send/receive/replay lag and preventing log recycling on the source.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: Physical pages or index structures are corrupt or mutually inconsistent, producing checksum failures, wrong-result reads, and apply/redo errors.

When all three faults are present simultaneously, the system exhibits an intertwined symptom set:  
• End-user transactions see sharply rising commit latency, intermittent "log full" or "cannot allocate new log segment" errors, and sudden throughput cliffs.  
• Replication monitoring shows ballooning send-, write-, and replay-lag; relay logs and retained primary log segments grow unchecked; failover readiness drops to zero.  
• Integrity checkers and query workloads report checksum failures, duplicate/missing rows, and replication apply errors such as "redo/row for missing page" or "index inconsistent with heap".  
• The primary’s log directory and the replica’s relay/redo directories expand simultaneously, checkpoint frequency spikes, and background archiver or apply processes cycle between idle, retry, and crash-restart states.  
• Because the same retained log segments are needed both for crash-recovery of corrupt objects and for lagging replicas, storage fills faster, further throttling log writes and widening replication gaps.

Causal chain: Corruption inside data blocks or index pages can cause the replica’s apply thread to halt or repeatedly retry the same failing redo, instantly creating a replication backlog. That backlog forces the primary to retain old log files, which consumes log-device space and intensifies the existing log-subsystem bottleneck; the resulting commit stalls generate even more drastic checkpoint and log-switch pressure, raising the chance of additional corruption during stressed I/O. Meanwhile, the saturated log path slows delivery of fixes (e.g., repairs, index rebuilds) to replicas, so corruption-induced apply failures persist and continue blocking log recycling. The feedback loop between log saturation, replication lag, and corruption-triggered apply errors amplifies each individual anomaly, degrading both write availability and read consistency across the cluster and leaving the entire estate vulnerable to data loss or extended outage.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
